packs.title: Curves and Open Sky
packs.promise: Read carved stone, collect a tiled wave and let an eastern waterfront view shift.

q.s: Turn a monument’s outline into three original lines.
st: From one stopped view, choose the monument’s tall vertical line, its sloping side and one small figure silhouette.
Make an original three-line drawing or three short lines of words: one upright, one angled and one small. Describe shapes rather than speaking for a historical person.
Save the composition and give it your own short title.

q.s: Find small repetitions in a broad curve.
st: Find a repeated ceramic shape, a broad roof curve and an area of shade beneath the overhang.
Draw or describe each at a different scale: small tile, large curve, dark opening. Do not touch the building or move toward the water to improve the view.
Save your three-scale collection. A written description works as well as a drawing or photo.

q.s: Build a small composition from stone and open space.
st: Choose a curved stone opening, a straight edge and a patch of sky or leaf space. Observe without standing in the road or arch passage.
Make an original three-shape composition with one curve, one line and one unfilled gap. Words describing the arrangement work as well as drawn marks.
Save your composition and name the space you deliberately left empty.

packs.title: Stone to the River
packs.promise: Find a Lisbon story in the paving, the open spaces and the river light.

q.s: Collect a moving pattern on a still square.
st: Choose a comfortable stopping place beside an open patch of Rossio’s black-and-white calçada portuguesa, the patterned stone paving.
Follow one dark wave with your eyes. Find where it bends one way and where it bends back.
Compare that wave with a neighbouring pale band. Collect a wide part, a narrow-looking part and one join where individual stones become easy to see.
Save the three details and describe how a flat pattern gives you a sense of movement.

q.s: Find how little shapes build a larger pattern.
st: From an open public place in Praça do Município, look at the patterned stone paving and the city hall façade.
Find a triangular unit in the paving, then follow the way neighbouring units build a larger shape. Choose a small group rather than trying to count the square.
Look up and find a different triangle on the building. Compare its scale and orientation with the one below.
Save the small paving shape, the larger pattern it joins and the triangle above.

q.s: Let four textures describe the riverfront.
st: Choose a comfortable public place on the upper promenade, well back from the river edge and outside commercial seating.
Pick four textures you can observe without touching: one in the paving, one in the water, one in planting and one in a distant surface. Colour or shape can stand in for a texture.
Write a four-line postcard with one texture in each line. Address it to an imaginary future version of yourself; begin each line with a different action word.
Read it quietly and change one word. Save the four lines and the view details that inspired them.
